title: Store: replace `ReadWriteNode`/`UnfrozenInternalNode` with plain nodes, hidden state and a dirty-read lock
body:
The node model from #6053 had three kinds of node: `FrozenInternalNode`, `UnfrozenInternalNode` and the `ReadWriteNode` class. Repeated upserts on a large parent also cost O(children) per call. This PR keeps nodes plain at every boundary userland sees. Store-only data goes into hidden private fields, and `hasPart`/`isPartOf` are updated by delta instead of being recomputed.

### Node model

- **Plain nodes everywhere.**
   - The graph holds frozen plain objects (`FrozenInternalNode`).
   - `createNode()` returns `DraftNode` (renamed from `UnfrozenInternalNode`): validated, with deep-frozen values, but the object itself is not frozen.
- **`private/draft.ts`** replaces the `ReadWriteNode` class with a plain `Draft` record plus functions:
   - `createDraft`, `readDraft`, `commitDraft`, `setDraftPartOf`, `removeDraftReferencesTo`, `getDraftReferenceIds`.
   - `commitDraft` freezes an owned node in place when possible. Otherwise it rebuilds the node in one O(properties) pass (no `delete`), keeps key order, and reuses a `FrozenNodeSet` whose IDs haven't changed.
- **`private/hiddenNodeState.ts`** stores the cached `dateCreated` time and sorted children as private fields, using the constructor-return trick.
   - They are invisible to `Object.keys`, spread and `JSON.stringify`.
   - If the stamp is lost (e.g. userland returns a `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(node))` clone), `getDateCreatedTime()` re-parses `dateCreated`.
   - Private fields benchmarked about 5× faster than a symbol property to attach (`npm run benchmark:node`).
- **Removed:** `ReadWriteNode`, `freezeNode`, `dateCreatedTime.ts` and the symbol-based sorted-children getter.

### `upsert()` semantics

- **Reads inside an updater:**
   - First read of a node in a transaction (clean read): the frozen node from the graph.
   - Later reads in the same transaction (dirty read): a new plain copy with the transaction's changes.
   - In both cases the node is frozen in `finally`, so it can only be changed inside its own updater.
- **No `upsert()` / `delete()` inside an updater.** Nested calls throw before any state changes.
   - The ban also covers code that runs while the store reads the returned object (getters, proxies).
   - Reading committed state (`getSnapshot()` etc.) is still allowed.
- **Identity fast paths.** If the updater returns the same `hasPart` / `isPartOf` it received, the store skips validating and diffing them. The nesting ban is what makes this safe: the sets shown to the updater are still current when it returns.
- **Child sets without copying.** The live child set is finalized and a new working copy is started on top, at O(changes) instead of the old O(children) copy.

```js
transaction.upsert(id, node => ({ ...node, text: ['Hi'] }));          // keeps the same hasPart: O(1)
transaction.upsert(id, node => {                                        // second read: writable here only
  node.isPartOf = new Set(node.isPartOf).add({ '@id': '_:other' });
  return node;
});
```

### `createNode`

- Throws if a node, a property-value item or a node reference has `toJSON()`, own or inherited. `toJSON()` is still called inside a JSON literal's `@value`.
- `hasPart` / `isPartOf` that are already a `FrozenNodeSet` skip valibot validation and are reused as-is (about 300 µs saved per 1,000 parts).

### Benchmarks

New store-level rows in `benchmark.ts`, plus a new `benchmark.node.ts` (`npm run benchmark:node`):

| Benchmark (100k nodes) | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Update parent (µs/op) | 88,279 | 12 |
| Repeat upsert (µs/op) | 104,658 | 9 |
| Mirror churn (µs/op) | 144,482 | 24 |

Other rows (Append, Random, Delete, Iterate, identifier rows, memory per node) are unchanged or slightly better. "Update parent add one" is still O(N), because the updater copies `hasPart` itself with `new Set(...)`.

### Trade-offs for review

- A later read in the same transaction always copies the node, at O(properties).
- Child sets are finalized mid-transaction. If the transaction then fails, the next commit that touches one of them pays a one-time O(size) copy.
- A node's references are not cached in the `Draft`; they are recomputed on every change at O(properties).

`OPINIONS.md` now documents the `toJSON` rule, the dirty-read lock and the hidden-state rebuild.
